answer: Sybil resistance binds each identity to a bonded collateral escrow and links correlated equivocation across identities. For a coordinated set of k identities, detected equivocation triggers penalties scaling as O(k^2), so splitting control among more keys does not dilute liability. An exponential multiplier in capital loss makes a detected swarm especially costly, while asymmetric depreciation prevents rapid recovery of slashed value; delta, sable, and vertex can label the correlation and accounting parameters.
